# Quarantine 2026-10 merge-group flake cohort (issue #3264)

## What changed

Seven merge-group flake detections from the issue #3264 cohort (plus its
comment batches, 2026-10-14 through 2026-10-20) are quarantined with full
OWNER/EXPIRY metadata (issue #2477 grammar, `check:invariants` Check 7),
after per-run evidence attribution from all eleven triggering CI runs:

- `scripts/ci/quarantined-tests-windows.txt` (+5; STATUS 3 → 8 active after
  the #3411 retirement of the 3-entry #3261 EBUSY cohort landed mid-PR —
  the branch was cut when the ledger held 6):
  `tests/unit/tools/test-runner-feedback-regressions.test.ts` (passed-on-
  retry on windows-latest three times in five days, the last after the
  2026-10-18 worktree-storm fixes), `tests/unit/full-auto/state-locking.test.ts`
  (hard failure 3/3 attempts: cross-process RMW worker exited 1 at
  `state-locking.test.ts:290`),
  `tests/unit/evaluation/runner-failures.test.ts` and
  `tests/unit/workflow/coder-settlement-2214-hardening.test.ts` (both
  post-storm-fix recurrences, 2026-10-19/20), and
  `tests/unit/commands/archive.test.ts` (re-add per the #2973 retirement
  re-add rule — fresh merge-group windows-latest failure).
- `scripts/ci/quarantined-tests-macos.txt` (+1):
  `tests/unit/plan/manager-current-phase-2532.test.ts` (passed-on-retry on
  macos-latest twice six days apart, the second post-storm-fix).
- `scripts/ci/quarantined-tests.txt` (+1):
  `tests/unit/background/plan-sync-worker.test.ts` (passed-on-retry on
  ubuntu-latest, 2026-10-20; ubuntu evidence routes to the general ledger
  because the coverage gate honors only that ledger — issue #2660
  precedent).
- `tests/unit/scripts/ci/ci-yml-quarantine-3264.test.ts` (new): companion
  ledger-pinning regression test (the #2761/#2826/#2867 pattern) asserting
  each of the seven entries is active in exactly its attributed ledger,
  carries the OWNER/EXPIRY block, exists on disk, the windows STATUS header
  stays honest (declared == actual, 8 at the shipped head), and same-basename sibling
  `tests/unit/evidence/archive.test.ts` stays in the gated set.

## Why

The flake-detection workflow filed the cohort, but the issue's own triage
comment asked that candidates be cross-checked against the triggering
merge-group runs rather than appended blindly. Every candidate was
attributed to its exact run/shard/OS via the check-run annotations API,
distinguished hard failures from passed-on-retry flakes, and checked
against post-detection root fixes:

- NOT quarantined, root-fixed on main: `guardrails-worktree-authority` and
  `guardrails-worktree-containment-hardening` (windows hard failures
  through 2026-10-18T15:06Z; the fixes `473df7e07` + `592e7b233` landed
  2026-10-18 and all three later merge-group runs execute both files
  green), and `tests/unit/hooks/w3368-diag-temp.test.ts` (deliberate
  fail-on-purpose diagnostic, deleted by `473df7e07`).
- NOT quarantined, watch list: the remaining storm-window candidates
  whose only evidence falls inside the 2026-10-14/18 windows teardown
  storms and which have been green in every run since (the 2026-10-14
  coverage-shard trio — `src/__tests__/cli-version.test.ts`,
  `src/commands/commands.test.ts`, `tests/unit/cli/run-command.test.ts` —
  was named in all four cohort issue bodies, a same-day four-detection
  cohort with zero recurrences in the 11 harvested runs through
  2026-10-20, and the coverage CORE-TREE pair), plus
  `pr-subscriptions-checkpoint.test.ts` (its storm-window retry satisfies
  the #2973 re-add rule's floor but is plausibly storm-correlated — left
  for human adjudication).
- One correction to that triage thread, whose attribution this fragment
  otherwise follows: its aside that the issue-body candidates "don't
  exist in the current tree — they only appear in docs/archive" is wrong
  — all six body candidates are tracked on `origin/main` with long
  history. They stay off the ledgers on evidence, not existence: zero

# Quarantine aging: retire the #3261 windows EBUSY cohort, renew the two expired entries (#3203)

## What changed

- `tests/unit/hooks/delegation-gate-rework-remediation.test.ts` and
  `tests/unit/hooks/delegation-gate-reentry-bypass.test.ts`: afterEach teardown
  now deletes the per-test temp dir through `safeRmRecursive`
  (`tests/helpers/safe-test-dir.ts`) instead of a raw `await fs.rm` with zero
  retries — the bounded EBUSY/EPERM/ENOTEMPTY retry pattern (~10 s budget,
  `closeProjectDb` first) already proven for the #2190/#2807 windows
  handle-contention class.
- `scripts/ci/quarantined-tests-windows.txt`: the three #3261 windows EBUSY
  entries are retired (6 → 3 active entries; STATUS header updated).
  `tests/unit/session/hydration-populate-guard.test.ts` — its named root fix
  (the same `safeRmRecursive` teardown routing) already landed in-tree via
  #3248 (commit 3bffa0295, pinned by
  `tests/unit/session/hydration-teardown-routing-3248.test.ts`); the two
  delegation-gate files above are root-fixed by this PR. The two entries whose
  named remedies could not be closed from CI evidence
  (`j02-failure-rejection-distinct`, `delegation-gate-background-coder`) are
  renewed to EXPIRY 2026-11-18 under the open #2973 cohort anchor, per the
  renewal-requires-issue policy (#2905).
- `tests/unit/scripts/ci/ci-yml-quarantine-2867.test.ts`: the pinned EXPIRY
  date moves 2026-10-20 → 2026-11-18 with the renewal.

## Why

Issue #3203 (quarantine-aging tracker, workstream #2905): four entries were
expiring within 21 days and two EXPIRYs were already past, putting Check 7 of
`bun run check:invariants` on course to hard-fail CI on 2026-11-01
(j02) and 2026-11-04 (delegation-gate-background-coder). Every entry needed
either a root fix or a policy-compliant renewal before its wall. The EBUSY
cohort's ledger criterion named this exact remedy ("root-fix the EBUSY
teardown (retry-with-backoff or platform-safe cleanup)"); the two renewed
entries had exhausted or already satisfied their named candidates
(delegation-gate-background-coder's `createSafeTestDir` conversion has been in
place since ec5bcceef, 2026-07-24), so renewal with an updated diagnosis under
the open cohort tracker is the honest action.

## Migration steps

None. The quarantine ledgers are CI-internal data files; no runtime or user
facing surface changes. The retirement is validated by this PR's own CI: the
diff touches `scripts/`, so detect-paths runs the full 3-OS unit matrix on the
PR (plus merge-queue), executing the three un-quarantined files on
windows-latest — the #2973 retirement-evidence precedent.

## Known caveats

- The windows EBUSY fix is validated by the PR's windows-latest matrix, not by
  a local windows host (not reproducible on Linux). If a retired file flakes
  again on merge-group windows-latest, re-quarantine narrowly per the ledger's
  re-add rule (fresh merge-group failure, not fixable at the root).
- The two renewed entries keep their quarantine until EXPIRY 2026-11-18; the
  tracker will re-file them as they approach that wall unless root-fixed
  earlier.

# feat(workflow): external-evidence task class + `/swarm attest` — an in-machine exit for git-external deliverables

## What changed

- Plan tasks can now declare `evidence_class: "external_git"` with pinned
  `evidence_anchors` (read-only git assertions like
  `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` expecting `0`). A new
  `/swarm attest <task_id>` command runs the anchors as bounded no-shell
  spawns and records a durable external-evidence bundle; completion is then
  admissible for that task WITHOUT any coder settlement ever existing — the
  in-machine exit for tasks whose deliverable is a commit/push or other
  git-external operation (previously permanently wedged: "Task N has no
  exact-task QA evidence" with `/swarm recover` a no-op).
- `save_plan` now warns when a commit/push-shaped task has an empty scope and
  no external declaration, naming both remedies (declare `external_git` +
  attest, or run it as a thin coder dispatch).
- `/swarm recover` distinguishes "no coder dispatch or settlement evidence was
  found" from a stuck settlement and lists concrete next steps (attest,
  manual close, thin-coder re-plan).
- Fail-closed by construction: undeclared tasks keep the byte-identical
  completion refusal; anchors admit only positively-known read-only git
  subcommands/flags (unknown flags, global options, `--output=`,
  `--show-signature`, `ext::` URLs, `status`/`ls-remote` all refuse); output
  beyond the evidence storage bound refuses instead of truncating; a
  declaration change revokes stale proofs (fresh attest required), while
  terminal evidence is preserved for audit.
- Plan hashes include the new optional fields (legacy plans hash
  byte-identically); `check_gate_status` and the plan/checkpoint markdown
  projections render the declaration.

# Fix: inherited-key lookups in lean-turbo scopes and /swarm concurrency, and numeric-entity decoding in web-fetch

## What changed

Same-class follow-ups to the `web_fetch` entity-decode fix, surfaced during review of that fix and closed in the same change set:

- `runPartitionPreflight` (`src/turbo/lean/partition-common.ts`) checked a caller-supplied `scopes` map with `task.id in scopes`. A plan task whose id was an inherited `Object.prototype` name (for example `constructor`) resolved to the `Object` function instead of a file list, and the planner threw `TypeError: ... is not iterable`. The lookup now uses `Object.hasOwn(scopes, task.id)`; a task id that is an own key of `scopes` still uses its declared scope, and any other id falls through to the normal undeclared-scope path (`.swarm/scopes/` file, then `files_touched` when `require_declared_scope` is false, otherwise the serialized no-scope path).
- `/swarm concurrency set <value>` (`src/commands/concurrency.ts`) checked presets with `normalizedValue in PRESETS`. `constructor` or `__proto__` matched, and the `Object` function was stored as the session concurrency override. The check now uses `Object.hasOwn(PRESETS, normalizedValue)`, so those inputs are rejected as invalid values.
- `decodeEntities` (`src/tools/web-fetch.ts`) now matches decimal references with `#[0-9]+` and hex references with `#x[0-9a-f]+`. Previously a decimal reference containing hex letters, such as `&#1e5;` or `&#12ab;`, was truncated by `parseInt` and silently dropped characters; it is now left as literal text. Numeric references that are NUL, a surrogate, or beyond U+10FFFF decode to U+FFFD (as the HTML spec specifies) instead of emitting a control character or lone surrogate, or vanishing. A digit run so long that it overflows to Infinity (hundreds of digits) is still left as literal text rather than decoded.

## Why

All three are the same class of bug as the main fix: a lookup or parse that accepts input it should reject, on values that originate from untrusted HTML or operator input. They sit next to the code the main fix touches, so they are closed here rather than left open.

# v2 context bridge keeps tool-call pairing for id-less host messages

## What

- On OpenCode V2, the `session.hook('context')` bridge (`onV2ContextEvent`) now stamps every v1 view with its index in the original `event.messages` (`info.swarmV2Origin`) and pairs each transformed view back to its v2 message by **object identity**, then **`id`**, then that **origin stamp**. There is no positional fallback.
- A message that carries non-text parts (tool calls, tool results, media) is not dropped when the chain drops its view (other than a consumed carrier source, below). Messages are rebuilt in the host's order.
- A message consumed as a guidance carrier source is removed from the list (its text is delivered once, in `event.system`), so each guidance unit has exactly one destination.
- Transformed text is written back **in position**, so an assistant's preamble stays before its tool call.
- Message content that is not an array (out of contract) is left untouched instead of being split or throwing.

## Why

The v2 host's context messages carry no `id`, so every message was paired back by position. The v1 chain changes the view count: `materializeSystemGuidanceInPlace` converts a mid-history system entry into a re-homed carrier, and other stages splice in verdicts. Every later view then landed on the wrong message and the trailing message was dropped. An assistant `tool-call` lost its `tool-result`, and the provider rejected the request (`unexpected tool_use_id found in tool_result blocks`). The guardrails retry rollback replaces every view with a `structuredClone`, which defeats identity pairing; the origin stamp is a plain string key, so it survives the clone.

## Migration steps

None.

## Known caveats

- On the v2 host, id-less views inserted by the v1 chain (the full-auto verdict and continuation messages) have no origin and are dropped. They are not delivered to the model. Previously they were written onto an unrelated message.
- The v1 host path and the v1 hook chain are unchanged.
- The live-run figures (2 of 5 runs failed before, 0 of 8 after, opencode 2.1.3, three-step shell scenario with opencode-swarm as the only plugin; 0 of 3 failed with a full plugin set) are the PR author's manual measurement taken before the origin-stamp change. They are not reproducible in CI.
<!-- custom-release-notes:end -->

# Honest INCOMPLETE lane settlement for PR reviews

PR-review workflows now settle their lanes truthfully instead of wedging: a
run that cannot finish validating can complete as INCOMPLETE with a durable
disclosure, lanes that produced provable evidence settle at collection time,
and the lane-liveness watchdog is on by default.

- **PR_REVIEW completion gains an honest INCOMPLETE exit** for COMPLETE and
  PARTIAL runs. When a reviewer/critic/council validation phase cannot
  settle, `complete_pr_workflow` may complete with `report_verdict:
  "INCOMPLETE"` once every lane is settled and the workflow is still bound
  to the PR head; the gate persists a durable validation-skip disclosure
  artifact (`.swarm/pr-review/<runId>/validation-skip-disclosure.json`) plus
  gate-state mirror fields before the terminal clear, and emits an audit
  event naming each skipped phase and its unsettled items. APPROVE and
  REQUEST_CHANGES are never admitted through this exit — an honest
  INCOMPLETE never claims code-quality approval.
- **Partial-coverage disclosure admission is retry-first**: while a
  contract-class failure still has unconsumed retry budget, the disclosure
  admission refuses and tells you to spend the retry first. Re-running
  affected dimensions after exhaustion supersedes the previously admitted
  disclosure only for the same dimension tuple, and every supersession is
  audited (`pr_review_coverage_disclosure_superseded`); a different
  disclosure tuple is still refused.
- **NO_COVERAGE completion retries reuse the admitted run id**, so a retry
  after a failed terminal clear replays the disclosure idempotently under
  the same `.swarm/pr-review/<runId>/` directory instead of minting a fresh
  id and colliding with the existing disclosure.
- **Cross-lane duplicate finding ids are rejected at receipt publish**:
  `submit_pr_review_result` refuses a finding id already claimed by another
  lane of the same run before any state write.
- **Stale-revision base dimensions disclose as PARTIAL**: under exhausted
  staged resilience, a base dimension whose lane settled against a stale
  revision is disclosed as PARTIAL coverage rather than blocking the
  settlement.
- **Verdict lanes settle on evidence instead of wedging**: lanes whose full
  transcript window carries a terminal message settle instead of failing
  `transcript_incomplete`; receipt-bearing lanes and idle empty-output
  lanes settle during collection; a stale/liveness verdict lane is
  superseded when a late valid transcript arrives (never for
  operator-cancelled lanes, discovery modes, or lanes cited by a persisted
  verdict-settlement receipt). Rejection errors now name the offending row
  first, with the full detail persisted as a lane artifact.
- **The lane-liveness watchdog is ON by default**: omitting the
  `lane_liveness_watchdog` configuration section now enables it (the
  30-minute deadline is unchanged). With the default config, a busy PR lane
  past the 30-minute deadline is now settled and its host session aborted
  (previously retained by the alive probe); opt out with
  `lane_liveness_watchdog.enabled: false` (the explicit opt-out path keeps
  working).
- **The architect prompt budget ceiling rises 164,000 → 165,000 chars**: the
  honest-INCOMPLETE completion guidance added here and the PR-feedback
  verification re-dispatch recovery that shipped in #3419 each fit under the
  old ceiling separately, but the merged prompt's feature-heavy cell measured
  164,188 — over by 188. The deliberate 1,000-char step keeps the #1649
  ratchet intact for unreviewed growth (docs/configuration.md updated).
